properties.natural_language: Before header validation begins via EDGE-START-VALIDATION, a block received from EXT-NETWORK-PEER must contain a well-formed header with parent hash, gas limit, timestamp, difficulty, and extra data fields present

After header validation passes via EDGE-HEADER-PASS, the block header has been confirmed to have valid parent hash, gas limit within bounds, monotonically increasing timestamp, correct difficulty, and extra data <= 32 bytes
The block validation pipeline must follow strict sequential ordering: header validation, then ommer validation, then body application, then root verification. No step may be skipped or reordered
Before ommer validation via EDGE-VALIDATE-OMMERS, the block must contain at most 2 ommer headers, each referencing a valid parent within the last 6 ancestor blocks
After root verification passes via EDGE-ROOTS-MATCH, the computed state root, transaction root, receipt root, and logs bloom must exactly match the values declared in the block header
Any validation failure at any stage (header, ommers, or roots) must result in STATE-BLOCK-INVALID with an InvalidBlock exception; no partial acceptance is permitted

After body application via EDGE-BODY-APPLIED, all transactions in the block must have been executed sequentially and the resulting state must reflect all balance transfers, storage modifications, and contract deployments
Before transaction validation via EDGE-CHECK-TX, the transaction from EXT-TX-SENDER must have a valid ECDSA signature, and the sender address must be recoverable from the signature

After transaction validation passes via EDGE-TX-VALID, the sender must have balance >= gas * gas_price + value, nonce must match account nonce, sufficient block gas must remain, and sender must be an EOA

The total ETH in the system must be conserved across the transaction lifecycle: gas_fee_deducted = gas_refund_to_sender + miner_payment, and no ETH is created or destroyed except through the defined reward mechanism
After nonce increment via EDGE-INCREMENT-NONCE, the sender's account nonce must be exactly previous_nonce + 1, preventing replay of the same transaction
Gas refund must be capped at min(gas_used/2, refund_counter), ensuring at least half the gas consumed is not refundable
After receipt creation via EDGE-TX-COMPLETE, the receipt must contain the state root, cumulative gas used, logs array, and bloom filter computed from the logs
Before PoW validation via EDGE-START-POW, the block header from EXT-MINER must contain a nonce and mix_digest field produced by the Ethash mining algorithm
After hashimoto computation via EDGE-VERIFY-MIX, the computed mix_digest must exactly match the mix_digest declared in the block header
The PoW verification must enforce that the hashimoto result is less than or equal to 2^256 / difficulty, ensuring the mining difficulty target is met
After difficulty calculation via EDGE-DIFFICULTY-READY, the computed difficulty must account for the timestamp delta adjustment and the difficulty bomb term 2^(block_number/100000 - 2)
Before gas limit validation via EDGE-CHECK-GAS, the block must declare a gas limit that is within parent_gas_limit +/- (parent_gas_limit / 1024) and >= 5000
After block reward distribution via EDGE-REWARDS-DONE, the miner must have received exactly 5 ETH + (5 ETH / 32) * ommer_count, and each ommer miner must have received ((8 - ommer_age) * 5 ETH) / 8
The gas limit minimum bound of 5000 must always be enforced; no block with gas_limit < 5000 may pass validation
Before gas availability check via EDGE-START-CHECK-GAS, the remaining block gas (block_gas_limit - block_gas_used) must be calculable from the current block execution state
The validation chain must be executed in strict order: gas availability, nonce match, balance sufficiency, EOA check. Any failure at any step must immediately transition to STATE-VALIDATION-FAILED
After EOA check passes via EDGE-VALIDATION-PASS, the sender account must have no associated code (code_hash == EMPTY_CODE_HASH), confirming it is an externally owned account
Before querying the RPC provider via EDGE-QUERY, the client must have a known trusted state root (e.g., from consensus layer) to verify proofs against
Before proof verification via EDGE-VERIFY, the response from EXT-RPC-PROVIDER must contain both the data payload and a Merkle proof; responses without proofs must be rejected
After proof verification succeeds via EDGE-VALID, the data has been cryptographically confirmed to be authentic against the trusted state root without requiring trust in the RPC provider
After proof verification fails via EDGE-INVALID, the data must be rejected and the provider must be flagged as potentially malicious via STATE-MALICIOUS-PROVIDER-DETECTED
No data from the RPC provider may be trusted without passing cryptographic proof verification; the path from EDGE-RESPONSE to STATE-DATA-TRUSTED must always pass through ACTION-VERIFY-PROOF
Before RLP-to-SSZ conversion via EDGE-RLP-TO-SSZ, the transaction must be a valid RLP-encoded transaction conforming to an existing transaction type envelope
After SSZ hash tree root computation via EDGE-ROOT-DONE, the resulting root must be deterministic: the same transaction input must always produce the same SSZ root hash
Partial proofs generated from SSZ tree structure must be verifiable against the root hash without requiring the full transaction data
Before receipt normalization via EDGE-NORMALIZE, the receipt from EXT-TX-EXECUTION must contain at minimum the status/state root, cumulative gas used, and logs
After receipt normalization via EDGE-NORMALIZED, the receipt must contain all fields needed for independent verification including logIndex and individual gasUsed per transaction
Before ETH transfer logging via EDGE-EMIT-LOG, the native ETH transfer from EXT-USER must have been executed successfully on the execution layer
After log query via EDGE-RETRIEVED, the returned logs must include a completeness proof demonstrating no additional matching logs exist beyond those returned
All native ETH transfers must be visible in the log data after EIP-7708 activation; no ETH transfer may occur without a corresponding log entry
The 2D log index must provide bounded false-positive rates for queries, ensuring efficient log retrieval without excessive scanning
After bloom filter removal via EDGE-BLOOM-GONE, the 2D index must fully replace bloom filter functionality with equal or better query precision
Before binary API deployment via EDGE-INEFFICIENT, the system must support SSZ encoding and Snappy compression capabilities
Binary-encoded blob data must be semantically identical to hex-encoded blob data; the encoding change must not alter data content
After database serving optimization via EDGE-DB-OK, SSZ data must be servable directly without runtime decompression overhead

Before deposit submission via EDGE-USER-SUBMIT-DEPOSIT, the EXT-DEPOSITOR must provide a valid 48-byte pubkey, 32-byte withdrawal_credentials, 96-byte BLS signature, deposit_data_root, and ETH value >= MIN_DEPOSIT_AMOUNT
After deposit_data_root validation via EDGE-DEPOSIT-ACCEPTED, the computed SSZ hash tree root of the DepositData must exactly match the supplied deposit_data_root parameter
The progressive Merkle tree must maintain correct incremental construction at DEPOSIT_CONTRACT_TREE_DEPTH=32, supporting up to 2^32 deposits without overflow
After DepositEvent emission via EDGE-EVENT-LOGGED, the event must contain the pubkey, withdrawal_credentials, amount, signature, and the correct deposit index
After beacon chain processing via EDGE-VALIDATOR-QUEUED, the validator must be placed in the activation queue pending further beacon chain processing
Before deposit submission via EDGE-ATTACKER-SUBMIT, any entity (including potentially malicious actors) can submit arbitrary pubkey, signature, and withdrawal credentials to the deposit contract
The deposit contract must NOT perform BLS signature verification; BLS validation is exclusively deferred to the beacon chain. The contract only performs deposit_data_root and amount checks
After beacon chain BLS verification fails via EDGE-BLS-INVALID, the deposit is silently ignored and the deposited ETH is effectively burned with no recovery mechanism
After beacon chain BLS verification succeeds via EDGE-BLS-VALID, the deposit has been fully validated including proof of possession of the BLS private key
Before calldata validation via EDGE-RECEIVE-CALLDATA, the EXT-DEPOSITOR must submit a transaction with calldata containing the deposit() function selector and encoded parameters

The validation pipeline must check in order: pubkey length (48 bytes), withdrawal credentials length (32 bytes), signature length (96 bytes), amount rounding, and deposit_data_root comparison. Any failure must revert the transaction
After deposit_data_root mismatch via EDGE-ROOT-MISMATCH, the transaction must revert entirely with no state changes and ETH returned to the depositor
Before message call processing via EDGE-TX-EXECUTOR-CALL, the EXT-TX-EXECUTOR must provide a valid Message object with caller, target, value, code, gas, and depth fields
After call type determination via EDGE-IS-CREATE or EDGE-IS-CALL, exactly one path must be taken based on whether the target address is empty (creation) or populated (call)
Both contract creation and message call paths must terminate at STATE-EXECUTION-COMPLETE with a valid MessageCallOutput containing gas_left, logs, and error status
Before collision check via EDGE-START-CREATE, the target contract address must have been computed from the sender address and nonce (CREATE) or sender, salt, and init code (CREATE2)
Contract creation must be atomic: if any step fails (collision, init code error, invalid code, insufficient gas), the entire creation must be rolled back to the pre-creation snapshot
After code validation via EDGE-CODE-OK, the runtime code must be <= MAX_CODE_SIZE bytes and must not start with byte 0xEF (reserved for EOF)
After successful deployment via EDGE-DEPLOYED, the contract's runtime code must be stored at the target address and the code deposit gas (GAS_CODE_DEPOSIT * code_length) must have been charged
Existing storage at the target address must be destroyed before init code execution, preventing storage collision attacks
The execution loop must always terminate: either by encountering a STOP/RETURN/REVERT opcode, an error condition, or running out of gas. Infinite loops are prevented by the gas mechanism
Before execution loop begins via EDGE-START-LOOP, the EVM frame must be initialized with pc=0, empty stack, empty memory, and the code to execute loaded
After an invalid opcode is encountered via EDGE-INVALID-OP, execution must immediately halt with all remaining gas consumed
Each opcode execution must advance the program counter; the fetch-decode-execute cycle must not allow the PC to remain static unless explicitly set by a JUMP instruction
The call depth must never exceed STACK_DEPTH_LIMIT (1024); any CALL/CREATE at depth >= 1024 must fail with StackDepthLimitError
After a nested call returns via EDGE-BACK-TO-PARENT, the call depth must be decremented back to the parent level and parent execution must resume correctly
Before depth check via EDGE-CALL-OPCODE, the current message depth must be a non-negative integer tracked in the EVM frame
Gas must be non-negative at all times: gas_left >= 0 must hold after every charge operation; any operation that would make gas negative must trigger OutOfGasError
After a gas refund is added via EDGE-REFUND-RECORDED, the refund_counter must be incremented by the correct amount for the storage clearing operation
After code deposit gas calculation via EDGE-DEPOSIT-CALC-DONE, the cost must equal exactly GAS_CODE_DEPOSIT (200) multiplied by the runtime code length in bytes
Before REVERT parameter reading via EDGE-ENCOUNTER-REVERT, the EVM must have at least 2 values on the stack (memory_offset and memory_length)
After REVERT completes via EDGE-ROLLBACK-COMPLETE, all state modifications made during this execution frame must be reverted and unused gas must be preserved (not consumed)
REVERT must always copy error data to the return data buffer before rolling back state; the caller must have access to the error message even though state is reverted
After insufficient gas for REVERT via EDGE-GAS-INSUFFICIENT, the execution must fall back to standard out-of-gas exception behavior consuming all remaining gas
REVERT gas cost must equal RETURN instruction cost; the only gas consumed is the cost of the operation itself plus memory expansion if applicable
After gas return to caller via EDGE-REFUND, unused gas must be credited back to the calling context, distinguishing REVERT from out-of-gas exceptions which consume all gas
After REVERT during contract creation via EDGE-DEPLOYMENT-ABORTED, no contract code must be stored at the target address and the caller's stack must receive 0 (failure indicator)
REVERT in CREATE/CREATE2 context must abort deployment completely; partial deployment (code stored but init code reverted) must never occur
Before jump destination popping via EDGE-JUMP-POP-DEST, the EVM bytecode from EXT-EVM-BYTECODE must have been loaded and valid_jump_destinations must be pre-computed
Jump destinations must be validated against the pre-computed valid_jump_destinations set; only bytecode positions containing JUMPDEST (0x5b) are valid targets
After an invalid jump destination is detected via EDGE-DEST-INVALID, execution must halt immediately via InvalidJumpDestError with all remaining gas consumed
After JUMPI condition evaluates false via EDGE-CONDITION-FALSE, execution must continue sequentially by incrementing the program counter by 1
The valid_jump_destinations set must be immutable during execution; no opcode execution may add or remove entries from this set
Gas costs for control flow opcodes must be fixed: JUMP costs GAS_MID, JUMPI costs GAS_HIGH, JUMPDEST costs GAS_JUMPDEST, PC/GAS cost GAS_BASE. These must be consistent across all implementations
After STOP execution via EDGE-HALT, evm.running must be set to False and execution must cease with no further opcodes processed
STOP opcode (0x00) must gracefully halt execution without consuming all remaining gas and without producing error output
Before sign request processing via EDGE-DAPP-REQUEST, the EXT-DAPP must provide a valid signerAddress, validatorAddress (20-byte Ethereum address), and dataToSign
The wallet must always display the validator address and data to sign to the user and obtain explicit approval before proceeding to sign; no signing may occur without user consent
After message construction via EDGE-CONSTRUCTED, the prefixed message must be exactly: 0x19 || 0x00 || validatorAddress || dataToSign, conforming to EIP-191 version 0x00
After signing via EDGE-SIGNED, the resulting 65-byte signature (r, s, v) must be a valid ECDSA signature over keccak256(prefixed_message) using the signer's private key
Before signature verification via EDGE-RECEIVE-SIG, the EXT-CALLER must provide a signature, claimed signer address, and the original data that was signed
The validator must reconstruct the message using its own address (not the claimed signer address) to ensure the signature was specifically intended for this validator
After ecrecover via EDGE-RECOVERED, the recovered address must be compared against the claimed signer address; match indicates valid signature, mismatch indicates invalid
The EIP-191 0x19 0x00 prefix must prevent cross-context signature reuse: a signature for validator A must always fail verification at validator B due to different hash computation
The 0x19 prefix byte must prevent signature reuse as a transaction; the EIP-191 format is structurally incompatible with RLP-encoded transactions
Before any signature reuse attempt by EXT-ATTACKER, the attacker must only have access to the signature bytes and public information; private key access would bypass all protections
Before transaction announcement via EDGE-READY-TO-SEND, the eth/68 message must contain correctly packed types byte array, sizes array, and hashes array with matching lengths
After metadata extraction via EDGE-EXTRACT-TO-BUILD, the transaction type must be correctly encoded as a single byte and the size must accurately reflect the encoded transaction length
The types, sizes, and hashes arrays in the announcement message must have equal length; each index position must correspond to the same transaction across all three arrays
Before announcement parsing via EDGE-PEER-ANNOUNCE, the announcement from EXT-ANNOUNCING-PEER must be a valid eth/68 message with types, sizes, and hashes arrays
The selective fetch decision pipeline must evaluate type, size, and bandwidth budget in order; rejection at any stage must result in skip decision without fetching the full transaction
After transaction fetch via EDGE-GET-TO-FETCHED, the full transaction data must be received and available for standard validation; the fetched transaction must match the announced hash
Before DoS mitigation via EDGE-ATTACKER-SUBMIT, the attacker from EXT-ATTACKER submits large transactions to the network attempting bandwidth exhaustion
Transaction size must be known before full data is fetched; the eth/68 size metadata must enable size-based filtering without downloading the transaction payload
After throttling policy application via EDGE-THROTTLE-TO-PREVENTED, the network-wide bandwidth exhaustion attack must be mitigated through per-peer and global bandwidth limits
After peer behavior tracking via EDGE-TRACK-TO-THROTTLED, peers announcing excessive large transactions must have reduced priority or be disconnected
Before RPC request processing via EDGE-CLIENT-SUBMIT-REQUEST, the EXT-RPC-CLIENT must provide signed transaction data and optional timeout parameter via JSON-RPC
After timeout validation via EDGE-TIMEOUT-VALID, the timeout must be a positive integer not exceeding the node-configured maximum; invalid values must fall back to node default
The synchronous wait must have a bounded duration; no RPC connection may be held open indefinitely. The timeout mechanism must always terminate the wait
After receipt is obtained via EDGE-RECEIPT-RECEIVED, the full transaction receipt must be returned to the client including status, gas used, logs, and block information
After timeout expiration via EDGE-TIMEOUT-REACHED, error code 4 must be returned to the client indicating the transaction was not processed within the timeout duration
After node unready detection via EDGE-NODE-UNREADY, error code 5 must be returned indicating the node cannot process the transaction due to missing nonce or insufficient funds
Before parameter validation via EDGE-CLIENT-SENDS-PARAMS, the EXT-RPC-CLIENT must provide transaction bytes in valid hex encoding format
Transaction data validation must occur before timeout validation; invalid transaction data must result in immediate error return without proceeding to timeout validation
After invalid timeout falls back via EDGE-DEFAULT-APPLIED, the default timeout (recommended 2 seconds) must be applied and processing must continue normally
Error codes must be deterministic: timeout always returns code 4, node unready always returns code 5, invalid transaction uses standard JSON-RPC error codes
After error response is sent via EDGE-SEND-ERROR, the RPC connection resources must be released and the synchronous wait must be terminated
Before timeout detection via EDGE-TIMEOUT-DETECTED, the node must be actively processing a transaction with an active timer tracking the timeout duration
Before input length check via EDGE-START-LENGTH-CHECK, the CALL to precompile address 0x09 from EXT-CONTRACT-CALLER must provide input data in the calldata
Input length must be exactly 213 bytes; any other length must trigger InvalidParameter exception. There is no padding or truncation tolerance
The final block flag (f) must be exactly 0 or 1; any other value at byte offset 212 must trigger InvalidParameter exception

After parameter parsing via EDGE-VALID-LENGTH-PARSE and EDGE-PARSE-TO-FLAG-CHECK, the extracted parameters must conform to EIP-152 format: bytes 0-3 = rounds, bytes 4-67 = h, bytes 68-195 = m, bytes 196-203 = t_0, bytes 204-211 = t_1, byte 212 = f
Gas cost must be exactly GAS_BLAKE2_PER_ROUND * rounds; the gas cost scales linearly with the number of compression rounds and is always deterministic
After insufficient gas detection via EDGE-CHARGE-FAIL, the precompile call must revert with OutOfGas exception and all gas must be consumed
The BLAKE2b compression function must produce exactly 64 bytes of output regardless of the number of rounds or input parameters
After compression completion via EDGE-SET-COMPLETE, the EVM output must contain the 64-byte result of the BLAKE2b compression function per RFC 7693
Before compression execution via EDGE-READY-INIT, all inputs must have been validated and the required gas must have been charged
The compression function must execute in bounded time proportional to the number of rounds; the computation must not exhibit non-linear resource consumption
